title: Daily Routines
description: Describe your daily schedule using reflexive verbs and time expressions. Learn the vocabulary for morning and evening routines.

vocabulary.source: to sleep / to go to sleep
to go to bed / to lie down

grammar.title: Reflexive Verbs in the Present
grammar.content:
Reflexive verbs describe actions that the subject does to themselves. They are formed with a reflexive pronoun (me, te, se, nos, os, se) + the verb conjugation.

Reflexive pronouns:
- me (myself)
- te (yourself, informal)
- se (himself/herself/itself/yourselves formal)
- nos (ourselves)
- os (yourselves, Spain informal)
- se (themselves/yourselves formal)

Example: 'Me despierto a las seis' (I wake up at six).

Conjugation of 'despertarse' in the present:
- yo me despierto
- tú te despiertas
- él/ella/usted se despierta
- nosotros nos despertamos
- vosotros os despertáis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes se despiertan
examples: Me despierto a las seis de la mañana. (I wake up at six in the morning.)
Ella se ducha después de levantarse. (She showers after getting up.)
Nosotros nos acostamos tarde los fines de semana. (We go to bed late on weekends.)
¿Te afeitas por la mañana o por la noche? (Do you shave in the morning or at night?)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian reflexive verbs also use pronouns (mă, te, se, ne, vă, se) before the verb: 'mă trezeam' = 'me despertaba'. The structure is the same — just swap the verb conjugation.

pronunciation.title: The Rolled R vs Single R
pronunciation.content:
Spanish has a single tap /r/ and a rolled trill /rr/. Understanding the difference is key to being understood.

Single /r/ (tap — one quick flash of the tongue):
- Between vowels: caro (expensive), perro (dog)
- At the start of a word: rojo (red), ramo (bunch)
- After consonants: azul (blue)

Double /rr/ or R at the start of a word (trill — multiple rapid flashes):
- Between vowels: perro (dog), cerveza (beer)
- At the start: rojo (red), Romeo

Tip: The rolled R requires airflow — place your tongue tip behind your upper teeth and blow air. It's like the sound a motor makes.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian also has a single 'r' sound that's similar to the Spanish tap. The rolled trill is an extra skill — practice with words like 'perro' (dog) vs 'pero' (but).

exercises.question: Match each Spanish daily routine verb with its English meaning:
exercises.explanation: These reflexive and regular verbs are key for describing your daily routine.

exercises.question: What is the reflexive pronoun for 'nosotros'?
exercises.explanation: 'Nos' is the reflexive pronoun for nosotros: 'Nos levantamos a las siete' (We get up at seven).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Yo me ____ (ducharse) por la mañana.' (I shower in the morning.)
exercises.explanation: 'Me ducho' — the yo form of ducharse in the present. The reflexive pronoun 'me' goes before the conjugated verb.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ellos se ____ (acostar) a las once.' (They go to bed at eleven.)
exercises.explanation: 'Se acuestan' — they go to bed. Acostarse has a stem change: o→ue in the present (ellos se acuestan).

exercises.question: Which of these is a reflexive verb for daily routine?
exercises.explanation: 'Despertarse' (to wake up) is reflexive — the action reflects back on the subject: yo me despierto.

exercises.question: Match the breakfast items:
exercises.explanation: These are common breakfast items you'll encounter in a Spanish-speaking household.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Por la ____ me levanto a las siete.' (In the morning I get up at seven.)
exercises.explanation: 'Por la mañana' means 'in the morning.' 'Por la tarde' = in the afternoon, 'por la noche' = in the evening.
